problems.description: Employees receive emails that appear to come from internal IT requesting credential updates. The messages contain malicious links that harvest login credentials when clicked.
risk_reduction: Enable multi‑factor authentication (MFA) for all user accounts
Deploy email filtering to flag or quarantine suspicious senders
Run regular security awareness training and phishing simulations

problems.description: The dataset represents email-based social engineering threats where malicious actors send deceptive emails designed to lure recipients into taking actions such as clicking on links or divulging sensitive information. Malicious emails often contain suspicious keywords related to urgent financial opportunities, fraudulent business offers, or impersonations of trusted entities, while benign emails contain normal informational or conversational content. The analysis focuses on classifying emails as malicious or benign based on subject and body textual content using NLP techniques.
problems.asset_targeted: End user trust and potentially sensitive personal or financial information

indicators_of_compromise: Presence of suspicious keywords or urgent phrases in subject lines (e.g., 'Part-Time opportunity - $2000/week')
Inclusion of URLs directing to potentially malicious websites
Impersonation of reputable institutions or individuals (e.g., fake bank officers)
Use of unsolicited financial offers or inheritance scams
Source metadata linked to known phishing/spam datasets (e.g., 'TREC-07', 'CEAS-08', 'Enron')
attack_patterns: Use of urgent or enticing subject lines to attract attention
Bodies containing multi-line text with embedded URLs and requests for action
Narratives involving financial gain or confidential transactions
Emails written in a conversational but suspicious tone with poor grammar or formatting
Absence of personalized or contextual metadata
normal_patterns: Subjects reflecting standard conversational or informational topics
Bodies comprising formal academic calls for papers, news digests, or technical discussions
Presence of mailing list footers, unsubscribe links, and standard formatting
Source metadata from neutral or trusted datasets (e.g., 'Ling', 'TREC-07')

risk_reduction: Implement advanced NLP-based email filtering to detect suspicious keywords and patterns in subject and body text
Use supervised machine learning classification models trained on labeled datasets to improve detection accuracy
Educate users on recognizing phishing attempts and verifying email authenticity before engaging
Incorporate metadata analysis such as sender reputation and source verification to complement content analysis
Encourage use of email authentication protocols like SPF, DKIM, and DMARC to reduce spoofing
problems.data_source_notes: The dataset is large (131,346 records) with consistent binary labels but limited examples of malicious samples in the provided subset. Source field is uniform in samples, potentially limiting generalization. Body text includes mailing list footers and unsubscribe links that may introduce noise. Lack of explicit metadata such as timestamps and sender email limits contextual analysis but the presence of known phishing dataset sources supports reliability.

schema_analysis.data_type: email message content with classification labels

malicious_indicators: presence of suspicious keywords or patterns in subject/body
label indicating malicious (e.g., label=1 if present)
source metadata if known to be associated with spam/phishing
benign_indicators: normal conversational or informational content in subject/body
source metadata from trusted or neutral sources

subject.description: The email subject line summarizing the message topic
typical_patterns: potentially suspicious subjects with urgent or phishing keywords

body.description: The full textual content of the email message body
typical_patterns: multi-line text with email headers, quoted replies, URLs, signatures
presence of technical logs or commands (in some cases)
advertisements or unsubscribe links (common in mailing lists)

label.description: Binary classification label indicating benign (0) or malicious (1)

source.description: Origin or dataset source identifier for the email message
typical_patterns: may indicate known source of emails

indicators.label: integer - 0 (benign) or 1 (malicious)
indicators.subject: textual features, keyword presence
indicators.body: textual content analysis, presence of URLs, suspicious patterns

suggested_schema.detection_method: Natural Language Processing (NLP) based classification using subject and body text features combined with metadata; supervised learning with label as ground truth
additional_fields: attachments - metadata about attachments if any

data_quality_notes: Labels appear binary and consistent but no examples of label=1 provided in sample records
Body text includes mailing list footers and unsubscribe links which may add noise
Source field is uniform in sample ('Assassin'), may need more diversity for generalization
No explicit metadata fields like timestamp or sender email present, limiting contextual analysis
Large dataset size (131,346 records) supports robust model training but requires preprocessing to handle noisy text
